As a growing business located in 6 states, Forge Health opened its doors to their new facility in Langhorne on Friday. Forge Health provides proven in-person and telehealth outpatient treatment for mental health, substance use, and associated trauma.

As the co-chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force in Congress, I understand the need fill a longstanding void in our mental health system for those with mental illnesses and in need of treatment.

Ensuring proper care for America’s youth is non-negotiable. Any youth treatment facility receiving federal funding should and must meet the standards of a qualified residential treatment program. 
 
At today’s @WaysandMeansGOP hearing, I addressed several critical issues plaguing our child welfare system, including improving programs like Title IV, empowering community organizations to help implement change, and the impact of the growing shortage of foster homes. I will always be a voice and champion for our youth, and we must use every tool at our disposal to ensure children across our nation are supported, safe, and secure.

One of the impactful initiatives made possible through this funding is the construction of a new emergency homeless shelter for @FSABucksCo, with comprehensive on-site services, including mental health and substance use treatment, Housing-First case management, nursing care, and wellness programming.
 
Since 1954, FSABC has been a cornerstone of our community, changing lives and providing hope for individuals and families. With the $2.9 Million I secured for this incredible project, FSABC will be able to double its shelter capacity, break down the barriers of waitlists, and ensure that no one is turned away from the critical support needed to rebuild their lives. Thank you to Julie Dees and the entire FSABC team for your unwavering dedication to our community. I'm proud to support you and look forward to continuing to work alongside you in our shared mission to strengthen our community.
